Sentence (English): I finally decided to purchase this after much deliberation due to developing arthritis in my fingers.
Comments (English): [ It's good enough to recommend to everyone around me~! ^^b ] || ---------------- || I finally decided to purchase this after much deliberation due to developing arthritis in my fingers. While many believe that bigger is better when it comes to dishwashers, based on my experience using built-in, "large-capacity" dishwashers for about 20 years, I found that I almost only used it when the whole family gathered for the holidays. I bought the 6-place setting model intending to use it for every meal, but now, even this can handle a surprisingly large amount of dishes—to the point where I only need to run it once in the evening! Installation was simple; I just threaded the water supply hose through the existing gas pipe hole, so no separate opening was required. Since drying alone can make a difference of about 20 minutes in runtime, and water isn't removed effectively depending on the material, I disable the drying function and use natural drying instead. I take plastics and wooden items, which don't dry easily, out immediately after washing and move them to a drying rack. The rest of the dishes are almost completely dry after just the high-temperature wash, and they tend to dry quickly. I initially cut the detergent packet in half, but I found that using 1/3 or 1/4 of it is sufficient. The most satisfying part about using this dishwasher is that the glasses get cleaned so thoroughly they squeaky clean. It also removes all kinds of food odors perfectly. I liked it so much after using it that I found myself recommending it to everyone around me. Recently, when my sister moved, I gifted her the exact same product as a housewarming gift, and my brother ended up buying one too, so now the whole family uses the "Samsung BESPOKE Countertop 6-Place Dishwasher." Even though it is a 6-place model, it is bulkier than I expected and takes up quite a bit of space, but the dishwasher's performance is so outstanding that I am willing to put up with that minor inconvenience. Of course, you still have to use your fingers to stack the dishes neatly, but compared to scrubbing hard to clean them thoroughly, it puts less strain on your fingers, so I am extremely satisfied! There really is a reason why everyone looks for the "Dishwasher Lady." ^^b -------------------- I hope this review was helpful. Thank you. ^^
Comments (Original): [ ◈ 주변에 추천할 만큼 좋아요~! ^^b ] || ---------------- || 손가락에 관절염이 생기면서 오랜 고민 끝에 구입하게 되었습니다. 식기세척기는 거거익선이라는 의견이 많지만... 약 20년 정도 빌트인 스타일의 '대용량' 식기세척기를 사용해 본 경험상, 거의 명절에 온 가족이 모일 때만 사용하게 되더라구요~ 매 끼니마다 사용할 생각으로 6인용을 구입했지만, 지금은 이것도 저녁에 한 번만 돌릴 정도로 생각보다 꽤 많은 양의 설거지가 가능합니다! ^^설치는 기존 가스배관 구멍에 급수호스를 통과시켜, 별도의 구멍이 필요치 않았습니다.  건조만으로 약 20분 정도의 가동시간 차이가 발생하기도 하고... 소재에 따라 물기 제거가 잘 되지 않는 경우도 있어서, 건조기능은 빼고 자연건조를 이용합니다.→ 잘 마르지 않는 플라스틱과 나무류는 세척 직후 꺼내서 건조대로 옮겨두고,  나머지 식기류는 고온 세척만으로도 거의 다 마른 상태 + 금방 건조되는 편입니다.세제는 처음엔 반으로 잘라서 사용했지만... 1/3 혹은 1/4로 잘라서 사용해도 충분하더라구요~ 식기세척기를 사용하면서 가장 만족스러운 부분은...  ▷ 유리잔들이 아주 뽀도독~할 정도로 깨끗하게 세척된다는 점이예요~ ▷ 각종 반찬냄새가 깔끔히 제거된다는 점도 있네요~  사용해 보고 너무 좋다보니... 주위에도 막 홍보(?)아닌 홍보를 하게 되더라구요~ 얼마 전 언니의 이사 때는 이사 기념으로 이것과 동일한 상품을 선물하였고... 오빠도 구입을 하게 되어서 온가족이 '삼성 BESPOKE 식기세척기 카운터탑 6인용'을 사용하게 되었답니다~ ^^ 6인용이라고 해도 예상보다는 부피가 큰 편이라, 꽤 많은 자리를 차지하기는 하지만... 그 정도의 불편함은 감수할 정도로 식기세척기의 효과는 탁월합니다. 물론 차곡차곡 넣을 때도 손가락을 사용해야 하지만, 깨끗하게 씻으려고 힘을 주며 설거지를 하는 것에 비하면 손가락에 무리가 덜 가다보니... 대만족입니다~!다들 식세기 이모님을 찾는 데에는 이유가 있더라구요~ ^^b  --------------------  ※ 후기가 도움이 되었다면 좋겠습니다. 감사합니다~♡ ^^

While many believe that bigger is better when it comes to dishwashers, based on my experience using built-in, "large-capacity" dishwashers for about 20 years, I found that I almost only used it when the whole family gathered for the holidays. I bought the 6-place setting model intending to use it for every meal, but now, even this can handle a surprisingly large amount of dishes—to the point where I only need to run it once in the evening! Installation was simple; I just threaded the water supply hose through the existing gas pipe hole, so no separate opening was required. Since drying alone can make a difference of about 20 minutes in runtime, and water isn't removed effectively depending on the material, I disable the drying function and use natural drying instead. I take plastics and wooden items, which don't dry easily, out immediately after washing and move them to a drying rack. The rest of the dishes are almost completely dry after just the high-temperature wash, and they tend to dry quickly. I initially cut the detergent packet in half, but I found that using 1/3 or 1/4 of it is sufficient. The most satisfying part about using this dishwasher is that the glasses get cleaned so thoroughly they squeaky clean. It also removes all kinds of food odors perfectly. I liked it so much after using it that I found myself recommending it to everyone around me. Recently, when my sister moved, I gifted her the exact same product as a housewarming gift, and my brother ended up buying one too, so now the whole family uses the "Samsung BESPOKE Countertop 6-Place Dishwasher." Even though it is a 6-place model, it is bulkier than I expected and takes up quite a bit of space, but the dishwasher's performance is so outstanding that I am willing to put up with that minor inconvenience. Of course, you still have to use your fingers to stack the dishes neatly, but compared to scrubbing hard to clean them thoroughly, it puts less strain on your fingers, so I am extremely satisfied! There really is a reason why everyone looks for the "Dishwasher Lady." ^^b -------------------- I hope this review was helpful. Thank you. ^^

Sentence (English): I am unhappy with the dishwasher - though that could be taken care of.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher might be ok, customer support is awful! ] || ---------------- || I am unhappy with the dishwasher - though that could be taken care of. Customer support is, however, HORRIBLE. I bought this dishwasher 6 months ago and from the beginning to door operated very roughly - felt like something was scraping. The release feature at the end of a cycle did not work because of that, only cracking the door about 1/2 inch. I thought it might break in over time but I finally called to have them take care of it - the unit is still under warranty. Samsung sent out a technician who confirmed that the hinges were the problem and then connected with Samsung HQ. After he showed them the evidence over a video call, the remote person declared \"physical damage\" saying that it would not be covered under the warranty. They offered no evidence of any physical damage. I've since called customer support and they have now shifted their reason for not covering it to \"installation error\" saying the space is too small. The tech who was here verified that there was ample space on either side of the dishwasher. Changing the reason for not honoring the warranty when they could not justify their first diagnosis is a pretty big smell. So in summary, the one year warranty is a total sham. They are simply saying that they will not honor the warranty.

Comments (English): [ Unhappy Customer ] || ---------------- || On June 3, 2023 My husband and I purchased a Ge Refrigerator and Ge Dishwasher. The Dishwasher has had problems that are causing me to miss days of work for service calls. Dishwasher model # GDP665SYNFS Model Series 600 Serial # HV789888. In February the trim around the control panel came off. I called for service and was scheduled for March 4, 2024. I took off work for a technician to come but instead received a phone call from GE to reschedule the service call. The call was rescheduled for March 5,2024 but I received a call from the technician asking what is the problem. After detailing the situation the technician decided to order the part in place of coming out. Scheduled for part installment March 8, no technician on March 11, the scheduled technician canceled and another tech came out. All days I have had to make concessions to my work schedule. This ordeal is making my kitchen useless and wasting my time from work. Within 3 weeks another service call was placed to GE because the lock light was on and would not release. After that the entire control panel went out we have not been able to use our dishwasher. Another service called was placed on Monday April 8,2024 I requested a afternoon time so I wouldn't miss work again. However the tech arrived early 1:00 pm. He stated the control panel went out and would continue to go out on this particular model. However, he wrote the finding up differently, He instructed me to call Consumer Relations for Ge regarding a replacement dishwasher. As a consumer I trust that when I purchase an appliance the maker will stand behind it. On Wednesday I reached out to consumer relations to request an exchange. Michelle took my call. She started out nice but was quick to let me know that she wasn't going to replace the dishwasher. At one point she became combative and aggressive. I tried to interject because Michelle would not listen. As I tried to explain the several defects with this particular model dishwasher, Michelle continued to over talk me. Many consumers have written in their reviews that they have experienced the same problems within a year of purchase for this model. This model seems to be defective and I am asking for a replacement dishwasher. April 18,2024 I am still waiting and washing my dishing. Customer support is, however, HORRIBLE.I bought this dishwasher 6 months ago and from the beginning to door operated very roughly - felt like something was scraping. The release feature at the end of a cycle did not work because of that, only cracking the door about 1/2 inch. I thought it might break in over time but I finally called to have them take care of it - the unit is still under warranty. Samsung sent out a technician who confirmed that the hinges were the problem and then connected with Samsung HQ. After he showed them the evidence over a video call, the remote person declared "physical damage" saying that it would not be covered under the warranty. They offered no evidence of any physical damage.I've since called customer support and they have now shifted their reason for not covering it to "installation error" saying the space is too small. The tech who was here verified that there was ample space on either side of the dishwasher. Changing the reason for not honoring the warranty when they could not justify their first diagnosis is a pretty big smell.So in summary, the one year warranty is a total sham. They are simply saying that they will not honor the warranty.

Sentence (English): Got this to replace a cheap Whirlpool dishwasher that broke after only a year.
Comments (English): [ Fantastic Dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || Got this to replace a cheap Whirlpool dishwasher that broke after only a year. We've had it for about 2 weeks now and it is a noticeable improvement. I like that it doesn't have a heating element in the bottom of the tank, so you can wash plastics on the bottom rack without worrying that they will melt or get damaged. The drying is phenomenal when you add rinse aid. Plastics are almost bone dry, which I don't think I've ever seen with any dishwasher before. Usually with other machines, there's a bit of water left on the top (like with reusable plastic containers/lids) but not with this machine. At first I thought it was silly that the dishwasher was wi-fi capable, but the app is actually well designed and gives you the current status of the wash cycle, and notifies you when it's done. Fairly easy to set up too. Overall I think this machine is a great choice. It's well designed, doesn't seem flimsy, and works really well.

Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-person L* dishwasher. After pre-washing, if there's little food, use half a tablet. (Based on a 12-person tablet) Drying: If L*'s water pressure is 100, Samsung's is around 90. When I used L*, it dried so completely at a high temperature that the dishes were so hot that it was hard to hold them. I didn't put any plastic in it. Samsung dries with high-temperature hot air, but the dishes don't get hot after drying. Maybe that's why the plastic doesn't deform, so I put all the plastic in. Samsung dries with 100-degree hot air, but at the end, the door automatically opens about 10 cm to release moisture and exchange heat? It seems to dry the remaining moisture in a way. In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say that plastic doesn't store heat? so it doesn't dry well. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. There were fewer water stains than I thought. It says to use rinse, but since it's an all-in-one detergent, I didn't need to use rinse. The stains were a little visible mainly on the large frying pan. For reference, the detergent brand I used is (Cascade*, Eco*, Nature*, Ecori*) and I threw it on the floor instead of putting it in the detergent container. Installation Those who are installing under a Samsung induction stove should first check with the installer, not the remodeler, to see if they have the materials to raise the induction. Since I also have a Samsung induction, the dishwasher technician brought the materials he had and raised the induction on the same day as the dishwasher installation. If the induction brand is different, you should raise the induction first and then install the dishwasher. This can take some time. They say that you don't need to raise the induction if the sink height is high. Samsung has two types of induction raising materials: 2cm and 4cm. My sink is not that low, so I raised it 2cm. Overall review I am so, so, so satisfied that I wonder why I bought a 12-person dishwasher now. I don't think I can go back to the days when I didn't have a dishwasher. If you remove the top shelf and use it, you can stack it high on the second floor, but I'm using it again in the third floor. I recommend using it in its original condition. 2. If you have a lot of plastic, download the plastic course from the download course and use it. It washes cleanly without any plastic deformation.^^ 3. There are days when the dishes have a strong fishy smell, and it was worse on the day I washed the egg and milk bowls. Put the bowls containing eggs and milk in the dishwasher after larval washing! Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-person L* dishwasher. I'll write about the differences first after purchasing and using a 12-person Samsung dishwasher. Washing: Samsung's water pressure is around 100, while L*'s is around 90. It may be the difference in the water flow between the 12-person and 6-person models. Without pre-washing, if there's a lot of food on it, use a whole tablet of detergent. After pre-washing, if there's little food, use half a tablet. (Based on a 12-person tablet) Drying: If L*'s water pressure is 100, Samsung's is around 90. When I used L*, it dried so completely at a high temperature that the dishes were so hot that it was hard to hold them. I didn't put any plastic in it. Samsung dries with high-temperature hot air, but the dishes don't get hot after drying. Maybe that's why the plastic doesn't deform, so I put all the plastic in. Samsung dries with 100-degree hot air, but at the end, the door automatically opens about 10 cm to release moisture and exchange heat? It seems to dry the remaining moisture in a way. In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say that plastic doesn't store heat? so it doesn't dry well. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. There were fewer water stains than I thought. It says to use rinse, but since it's an all-in-one detergent, I didn't need to use rinse. The stains were a little visible mainly on the large frying pan. For reference, the detergent brand I used is (Cascade*, Eco*, Nature*, Ecori*) and I threw it on the floor instead of putting it in the detergent container. Installation Those who are installing under a Samsung induction stove should first check with the installer, not the remodeler, to see if they have the materials to raise the induction. Since I also have a Samsung induction, the dishwasher technician brought the materials he had and raised the induction on the same day as the dishwasher installation. If the induction brand is different, you should raise the induction first and then install the dishwasher. This can take some time. They say that you don't need to raise the induction if the sink height is high. Samsung has two types of induction raising materials: 2cm and 4cm. My sink is not that low, so I raised it 2cm. Overall review I am so, so, so satisfied that I wonder why I bought a 12-person dishwasher now. When I used a 6-person dishwasher, I wasn't very impressed because I only put in dishes and had to wash pots by hand, but with the 12-person dishwasher, I can put everything in, so I'm not afraid of washing dishes anymore. I don't think I can go back to the days when I didn't have a dishwasher. Completely satisfied 10000000 Additional review It's been about 2 months since I bought it, and I'm gradually getting the hang of putting the dishes in. 1. If you remove the top shelf and use it, you can stack it high on the second floor, but I'm using it again in the third floor. I recommend using it in its original condition. 2. If you have a lot of plastic, download the plastic course from the download course and use it. It washes cleanly without any plastic deformation.^^ 3. There are days when the dishes have a strong fishy smell, and it was worse on the day I washed the egg and milk bowls. Put the bowls containing eggs and milk in the dishwasher after larval washing! Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-person L* dishwasher. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-person L* dishwasher. When I used L*, it dried so completely at a high temperature that the dishes were so hot that it was hard to hold them. I didn't put any plastic in it. Samsung dries with high-temperature hot air, but the dishes don't get hot after drying. Maybe that's why the plastic doesn't deform, so I put all the plastic in. Samsung dries with 100-degree hot air, but at the end, the door automatically opens about 10 cm to release moisture and exchange heat? It seems to dry the remaining moisture in a way. In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say that plastic doesn't store heat? so it doesn't dry well. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. There were fewer water stains than I thought. It says to use rinse, but since it's an all-in-one detergent, I didn't need to use rinse. The stains were a little visible mainly on the large frying pan. For reference, the detergent brand I used is (Cascade*, Eco*, Nature*, Ecori*) and I threw it on the floor instead of putting it in the detergent container. Installation Those who are installing under a Samsung induction stove should first check with the installer, not the remodeler, to see if they have the materials to raise the induction. Since I also have a Samsung induction, the dishwasher technician brought the materials he had and raised the induction on the same day as the dishwasher installation. If the induction brand is different, you should raise the induction first and then install the dishwasher. This can take some time. Overall review I am so, so, so satisfied that I wonder why I bought a 12-person dishwasher now. I don't think I can go back to the days when I didn't have a dishwasher. If you have a lot of plastic, download the plastic course from the download course and use it. It washes cleanly without any plastic deformation.^^ 3. There are days when the dishes have a strong fishy smell, and it was worse on the day I washed the egg and milk bowls. Put the bowls containing eggs and milk in the dishwasher after larval washing! In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say that plastic doesn't store heat? so it doesn't dry well. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 6-person L* dishwasher. After pre-washing, if there's little food, use half a tablet. (Based on a 12-person tablet) Drying: If L*'s water pressure is 100, Samsung's is around 90. When I used L*, it dried so completely at a high temperature that the dishes were so hot that it was hard to hold them. I didn't put any plastic in it. Samsung dries with high-temperature hot air, but the dishes don't get hot after drying. Maybe that's why the plastic doesn't deform, so I put all the plastic in. Samsung dries with 100-degree hot air, but at the end, the door automatically opens about 10 cm to release moisture and exchange heat? It seems to dry the remaining moisture in a way. In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say that plastic doesn't store heat? so it doesn't dry well. Since the plastic still had moisture, I just washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. There were fewer water stains than I thought. It says to use rinse, but since it's an all-in-one detergent, I didn't need to use rinse. The stains were a little visible mainly on the large frying pan. For reference, the detergent brand I used is (Cascade*, Eco*, Nature*, Ecori*) and I threw it on the floor instead of putting it in the detergent container. Installation Those who are installing under a Samsung induction stove should first check with the installer, not the remodeler, to see if they have the materials to raise the induction. Since I also have a Samsung induction, the dishwasher technician brought the materials he had and raised the induction on the same day as the dishwasher installation. If the induction brand is different, you should raise the induction first and then install the dishwasher. This can take some time. They say that you don't need to raise the induction if the sink height is high. Samsung has two types of induction raising materials: 2cm and 4cm. My sink is not that low, so I raised it 2cm. Overall review I am so, so, so satisfied that I wonder why I bought a 12-person dishwasher now. When I used a 6-person dishwasher, I wasn't very impressed because I only put in dishes and had to wash pots by hand, but with the 12-person dishwasher, I can put everything in, so I'm not afraid of washing dishes anymore. I don't think I can go back to the days when I didn't have a dishwasher. There are days when the dishes have a strong fishy smell, and it was worse on the day I washed the egg and milk bowls. Put the bowls containing eggs and milk in the dishwasher after larval washing! Sentence (English): I used a 6-person L* dishwasher before.
Comments (English): [ Another new world after clothes dryers ] || ---------------- || I used a 6-person L* dishwasher before. I'm using the 12-person Samsung dishwasher now, and I'll write about the differences first. Washing. Samsung's is around 100 degrees, while L*'s is around 90 degrees. This may be due to the difference in water flow between the 12-person and 6-person models. If there's a lot of food on the clothes without pre-washing, I use a full tablet. If there's less food after pre-washing, I use half a tablet (based on a 12-person tablet). Drying. L*'s is 100 degrees, while Samsung's is around 90 degrees. When I used L*, the dishes came out completely dry at high temperatures, so hot that they were hard to hold. I didn't put any plastic in them. Samsung's is a high-temperature hot air dryer, but the dishes don't get hot after drying. Maybe that's why the plastic doesn't warp, so I put all of them in. Samsung dries with 100-degree hot air, and towards the end, the door automatically opens about 10 centimeters to release moisture and heat exchange? It seems to dry the remaining moisture in this way. In fact, when I opened it about an hour after the automatic door opened, everything except the plastic was dry. They say plastic doesn't store heat? and so it doesn't dry well. The plastic still had moisture, so I washed it in the dishwasher and dried it separately in the dishwasher. Washed dishes. Of the dishes I put in the dishwasher, the Corelle dried the most completely without moisture. Water stains. I think water stains will vary depending on the detergent you use. There were fewer water stains than I expected. It says to use conditioner, but since it's an all-in-one detergent, I didn't need to. The stains were slightly visible, mainly on the large frying pan. Detergent brand. For reference, the detergents I used were (Cascade, Eco, Nature, Ecori). I threw them on the floor instead of putting them in the detergent container. Installation. Comments (English): [ Quiet and holds a lot! ] || ---------------- || We've been very pleased with our KitchenAid dishwasher after purchasing it nearly 3 months ago. Sentence (English): This is almost perfect.
Comments (English): [ Almost perfect dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This is almost perfect. I've never had dishes come out so clean, even baked on crusty pans are sparkling clean. Nearly silent, only the glow of the indicator light on the floor lets you know it's running. Love not having a heating element so no risk of anything melting, and the crystal dry system ensures that even plastic is dry when you are unloading. Honestly, there are probably too many special cycles that I won't ever use, but the half load is helpful now that we are empty nesters. The only issue is the design of the upper rack. Top third rack is adjustable and wonderful for flatware, large spoons, knives, etc. The bottom rack provides lots of space for plates, but can be a little challenging for baking pans without having them take up too much space. But that upper rack, which in our previous dishwasher would fit lots of cereal bowls, coffee mugs and glasses, is so oddly designed that you can only fit in a few bowls, and since it isn't centered, when you fill it with bowls, you can't load glasses beside them without them touching and possibly scratching. The "tilt" that is to help mugs not have water sitting on the top, means that even fewer glasses/mugs can go on that side. Still trying to figure out the best way to get things to fit. As for purchasing from CostCo, we decided that the free delivery, installation and removal of old appliances was a great benefit, only to learn that they wouldn't install a dishwasher and they wouldn't disconnect and haul off an old one. So we got it delivered only to then have to schedule someone else to haul off the old one and install the new one. And because the delivery is based on a multi-hour window it was hard to know when to schedule the installer.

Samsung sent a new rack, because the warranty on those is 5 years, but in short order the teeth on that one started breaking off too. I'm seriously thinking of junking this one and buying a Bosh.

Sentence (English): Unit is very quiet and seems to get the dishes pretty clean.
Comments (English): [ Great value, good quality, couple of shortcomings ] || ---------------- || Unit is very quiet and seems to get the dishes pretty clean. The installation service was fantastic, and I love the fact that Costco includes this (and haul-away and accessories) in their price, making this unit a great value! There are two shortcomings (one of which I knew about before I bought it) that I would mention. First, the unit doesn't dry the dishes very well at all. On a scale of 10, I'd give it a 4 in that department. The other shortcoming is that I prefer to have the silverware rack in the door because it's much easier to drop silverware in a door-mounted basket than it is to have to open the door fully, roll the bottom rack out, and put the silverware in. For many years, Whirlpool made dishwashers with this feature and we have purchased their product specifically for that feature. Unfortunately, the product designers at Whirlpool decided to drop that great feature from all their dishwashers (a huge mistake IMO). But as I said, I knew that before I purchased the unit. Overall, however, I'm very pleased so far with this purchase.

Sentence (English): I am delighted with the performance of our new Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Nearly Perfect ] || ---------------- || I am delighted with the performance of our new Bosch dishwasher. It replaces a previous model we owned for nearly twelve years. The reason we replaced the old one was that the controls were placed on a "pocket handle" used to open the tub. When the handle, which was made of plastic, broke after many years of use, the buttons controlling dishwasher operation fell out, and our control over some of the features of the unit was compromised. Bosch designers have moved the control buttons on our new appliance to a safer location in the upper edge of the door. So the reason we needed to replace our old dishwasher was satisfied. The machine cleans the toughest and most demanding jobs we have given it. Our dishes come out thoroughly cleaned and dried--even the baking dishes with baked-on residue. The unit is so quiet as to be inaudible. When we first got our new dishwasher I thought it was not running. Now I have come to appreciate its nearly silent operation. We are quite well pleased with both its performance and its appearance. Now I shall nitpick. I am persuaded that for a full was cycle (not the quick cycle) a small amount of dishwasher detergent is helpful. Previously we owned machines with an open recess beside the detergent cup door that allowed a small amount of detergent into the first burst of wash water, the so-called "pre-wash." Our new dishwasher does not have such a recess. In fact, the complementary supply of detergent that came with our dishwasher consisted of little Electrosol tablets, preventing me from adding any detergent to the pre-wash cycle. A related complaint concerns the marks dividing the detergent cup into thirds. These marks suggest that for small loads or lightly soiled dishes one might use less detergent. A great idea! Since the detergent cup on our Bosch seems to be made for tablets, however, it is impossible to use less soap than the packet contains. Our area does not have hard water, and often we can get by without filling the detergent cup to capacity. Perhaps more attention can be given to this wonderful capability in the literature accompanying the dishwasher. Please forgive my rant. I have given more space to a small idiosyncratic issue than is warranted. It's a great dishwasher. In fact, it's almost perfect.

Sentence (English): We regretfully had to replace our 22 year old portable dishwasher, which was working great but got too rusty for us to continue using it.
Comments (English): [ Residue on dishes, Soap in base ] || ---------------- || We regretfully had to replace our 22 year old portable dishwasher, which was working great but got too rusty for us to continue using it. This very expensive replacement has been very disappointing so far. :(There's been a lingering plastic/fishy smell since we received the dishwasher 2 months ago - it was worse at first, so I'm assuming it's off-gassing, but it's gross and smells every time it is run. Worse though, all of our dishes come out feeling slick - as if there's residue leftover on them. I switched detergents today thinking that might be the problem, but all that my new detergent revealed was that it must not be rinsing or draining well, because there were tons of suds in the bottom of the dishwasher after a 3-hour cycle. Currently running a second cycle with no soap to try to get the dishes clean.I have been wondering if because the dishwasher doesn't have a heated dry, my dishes actually just have a very thin layer of moisture on them causing the 'slickness'. But just today I noticed it on a bowl that had been washed over 24 hours ago, so I think it must be mostly residue.Hoping there might somehow be a fix for these issues, but not holding my breath. One of the other reviews said it well, they don't make them like they used to! :(

Sentence (English): Overall this dishwasher does the job, however, in comparison to the 2008 Whirlpool we replaced it falls short of expectations.
Comments (English): [ Wanted to love it, but.  ] || ---------------- || Overall this dishwasher does the job, however, in comparison to the 2008 Whirlpool we replaced it falls short of expectations.I will start with the good: It looks nice and is easy to use. It holds more dishes than our previous dishwasher, and the 3rd rack is great. The adjustable racks are quite handy, and it is definitely quieter than the model we replaced.We received the first unit, and upon initial use we were shocked by the amount of water remaining on dishes when the cycle finished. We spent a couple of weeks playing around with the settings, and were able to improve the drying capabilities a bit. However, the fan drying technology just simply doesn't dry the dishes. The fan would also run for 6+ hours if you didn't open the dishwasher to stop the fan despite the cycle having finished. After going back and finding consumers with the same reported issue, we decided to have the first unit replaced. -it sounds like there are a lot of inconsistencies in quality and functionality of this model due to the fan drying technology. Well. the second unit performed WORSE than the first. Changing the cycle settings and dryer settings didn't improve the drying process, and there is food residue remaining on the dishes after every load (despite rinsing before going through the dishwasher), as well as a small bit of food splatter that is stuck to the door of the dishwasher which has remained after 3+ cycles (I left it there to see if it would take care of itself since we use daily). This was not an issue on the first unit that was installed and in use for 2-3 weeks. Lastly, the drawers on the second unit are flimsy and do no roll smooth, but this was not an issue with the first unit we had.All-in-all, I can't recommend this model and we are so thankful we purchased from Costco as we have had to utilize the concierge service and 90-day satisfaction guarantee. We have ultimately decided to exchange for a new model altogether.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher was installed in mid-March, and I've used it at least 8 times since then - it's just me, but I cook a LOT, so I can produce enough dirty dishes in a couple of days to warrant its use.
Comments (English): [ An excellent dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher was installed in mid-March, and I've used it at least 8 times since then - it's just me, but I cook a LOT, so I can produce enough dirty dishes in a couple of days to warrant its use. Gets everything squeaky clean, although the "Normal" wash/dry cycle is longer than I had expected. It's MUCH quieter than my previous 18-20yo Whirlpool ADA-compliant dishwasher installed by previous owner. This one is not ADA-compliant, so there's more room between the racks, and I really do like the extra space it affords, but you have to bend further down to put things in the bottom rack. Not crazy about how the upper rack is configured (except that it accepts wineglasses! ); I've had to finagle a bit more to be able to fit some dishes in there, but the bottom rack has TONS of room and allows for easier insertion of larger dishes like platters and pots and pans (which I never used to put in my old dishwasher). Sentence (English): Clearly, my new dishwasher is a carefully manufactured and exceptionally thoughtfully designed piece of equipment.
Comments (English): [ Mixed Opinions ] || ---------------- || Clearly, my new dishwasher is a carefully manufactured and exceptionally thoughtfully designed piece of equipment. There is a "but" though. The controls are not user-friendly, nor intuitive. The objective is to be able to conveniently load the dishes, install some washing solution, successfully turn the machine ON And after a reasonable amount of time, be able to unload clean dishes. Sometimes it just won't turn on. Sometimes the machine climbs it once additional drying solution, but it's already filled to the brim. Sometimes the touch panel operates erratically; that is it doesn't respond to a touch at all. Together my wife and I have watched the numerous videos. We have listened to the tips and how to operate, and how to load a machine successfully. After using the machine for six months, it still seems to be a somewhat uninvited guest in our kitchen. On the plus side, when the indent piece of equipment chooses to actually work, the dishes do come out clean and sparkling. We haven't given up yet on this engineering marvel. We invested our time and energy in selecting this highly recommended machine. Hopefully, it will eventually become a comfortable, trusted member of our kitchen, appliance family. After six months of trying, our frustrated operational experiences with this machine do persist.

Sentence (English): I bought the Bosch dishwasher to replace my Kitchenaid.
Comments (English): [ I bought it for reliability ] || ---------------- || I bought the Bosch dishwasher to replace my Kitchenaid. The Kitchenaid needed to be fixed in six years. That's pretty pricey. I looked up reviews on Consumer Reports. Kitchenaid got a 5/5 on reliability while the Kitchenaid got 3/5. It's doing a great job cleanining the dishes and I love how it pops open when it's done. There's an app to control it over the wifi. Unfortunately, the UI is rather convoluted and not quick and simple to use. So I prefer to use the buttons on the machine itself. I love that the door pops open when it's done. However, it gets low points and the rack system. All the tines on the lower shelf are at an angle which makes it less flexible in ways to load dishes. I give that 2/5. The Kitchenaid had excellent racks that were very easy to load.

Comments (English): [ Quiet! Some problem solving. ] || ---------------- || Delivery was an ordeal, but tmay have been LG subcontractor. They kept dropping it while taking it off the truck, so make sure you check over the washer closely as you have only 48 hours to notice a problem. By the time I got it installed, I saw it was wet inside and thought it was used. LG said it was normal due to testing before leaving the factory. Installed easily except for the sound insulation that goes under the door by the kick plate. The instructions were bad so find the Youtube video for the LG dishwasher sound insulation kit and follow that. It's simple and makes a big difference. The installer couldn't figure that out. In fact the installer told me it was impossible to remove the old washer, to install this one and all sorts of things. He was a delivery man who installs.Love the features though I haven't used a lot of them in the first few months of owning. Ours arrived with a lower rack that wouldn't stay on track, the wheels were too close together. Customer service was great once I went through all the problem solving, they sent another rack that works like a dream.Love the flexibility of half the tines being able to go up or down for different ways of loading. It was awkward getting to an efficient process, but we're there now. It holds more than our previous one per load due to the flexibility. It never gets the dishwasher entirely dry, though my dishes are mostly dry.The top rack is handy, though we still keep forgetting to empty it until we need something from it. It's nice to be able to adjust the height of the middle rack and it does so fairly easily. Nervous about breaking it though so I avoid it.It was so quiet I wasn't sure it was working at all, but due to the bottom rack not staying on track, we thought the sound insulation sheet was too large to allow the door to stay open flat and that it was the reason for the rack going off track. The plate was cut to fix the problem only to find it wasn't the problem in the first place. As I said, the installation directions for it were so bad we didn't know. Trying to find another has been impossible. LG claims it's from the store or delivery people. Store doesn't know what it is. Delivery people say it's been over 30 days so can't help. (Took longer than 30 days to get it installed.) But I feel LG caused the problem with a faulty rack and poor directions so should send another, yet they have no part number for it. It does make a huge difference in the sound so be sure yours is done right and was delivered. It comes in a roll separate from the dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Good dishwasher, but not amazing.
Comments (English): [ Decent dishwasher for the cost ] || ---------------- || Good dishwasher, but not amazing. The 3rd rack doesn't get things as clean as the lower racks, but you lose space in the 2nd and 1st rack. My old washer fit all my pans, this one only accepts big pots in one spot. It demands more water (water pressure to kitchen sink is reduced while it's running) than my old one did, but the dishes aren't cleaner. It does dry well. The express setting takes about an hour/ 75 minutes, and the regular wash about 2.5 hours. I hope it holds up.

Sentence (English): We purchased this when renovating our kitchen, as the dishwasher we had before this was already 7-8 years old and worked best on Heavy Duty mode, but otherwise fine.
Comments (English): We purchased this when renovating our kitchen, as the dishwasher we had before this was already 7-8 years old and worked best on Heavy Duty mode, but otherwise fine. I do like the stainless interior and LOVE the third rack at the top for cooking tools, lids, and other flat items. It cleans very well, so no complaints there. If I were to pick apart anything, it does not feel as hefty as our old dishwasher so my mindset, which may be totally off base, equates that to flimsy or inferior. It has only be installed for less than 3 weeks and runs fine, so that assumption has been unfounded. I will say the bottom rack is very lightweight and easily goes out of alignment when being moved. Time will tell.

Sentence (English): We just returned this machine after 6 weeks (Thank you Costco! ).
Comments (English): [ Unhealthy "New Car Smell" lasted +50 washes ] || ---------------- || We just returned this machine after 6 weeks (Thank you Costco! ). Newly installed, it emitted a very strong plasticky odor, like "New Car Smell." Just "outgassing" I thought, as many products do these days, when they are new. The fumes were overwhelming when expelled with the steam of the hot part of the cycle. Bosch told us it would go away in a few washes. But 20 washes later it was still very strong (although a little less than at the beginning). We ended up running it about FIFTY (50) times before returning it -- and the unhealthy-smelling odors were still there. I suspect different people notice it more than others, but for me they were strong fumes that smelled chemical-like and "poisonous." The smell stuck to our dishes -- I'm concerned about what we were ingesting! What was it? Most likely "bitumen," a tarry asphalt-like substance that Bosch - and nearly all - dishwashers use now to insulate and dampen sound. The fumes from the bitumen are strongest when it gets hot. If you ask Bosch (as we did), they will tell you that their dishwashers do not CONTAIN contain bitumen. Which is technically correct - it isn't IN their dishwashers. It is in the INSULATION around their dishwashes. So who makes a dishwasher now without bitumen insulation? I have no idea. Repair guys tell me they all have it. I don't want to hand wash dishes for the rest of my life! We had a fabulous non-smelly Bosch before this that lasted 14 years. I recommended the brand to anyone who asked. Apparently, our purchase was just before they started using bitumen routinely. Whoever thought that our air could be poisoned by our dishwashers?

If you ask Bosch (as we did), they will tell you that their dishwashers do not CONTAIN contain bitumen. Which is technically correct - it isn't  IN their dishwashers.  It is in the INSULATION around their dishwashes. So who makes a dishwasher now without bitumen insulation? I have no idea.  Repair guys tell me they all have it. I don't want to hand wash dishes for the rest of my life!We had a fabulous non-smelly Bosch before this that lasted 14 years.  I recommended the brand to anyone who asked.  Apparently, our purchase was just before they started using bitumen routinely. Whoever thought that our air could be poisoned by our dishwashers?

Due to the limited space in the dishwasher, we find we have to hand wash larger items, when we have a party. This dishwasher might not be a good fit for a family but for the two of us it takes care of our needs.

I totally recommend the Bosch 500 Dishwasher!

Sentence (English): I've been using the machine for a few months.
Comments (English): [ No recommendation ] || ---------------- || I've been using the machine for a few months. The biggest problem is that the dishes are far too close together. Soup bowls with leftover oatmeal only get clean if I always leave a space between them. Even rinsing them immediately doesn't help, the washing water just doesn't seem to reach them. Melitta Ceracron flat plates (slightly raised edge) don't fit in at all. The distance between the wires is too small! I noticed this too late, as I use it as a spare set of dishes. The shelf on the left can only be locked at 45 degrees, so you keep getting stuck when putting things away. What were the designers thinking? In the pre-series (Generation Piccolo), where they were at the back, you could fold them up all the way. In the automatic program, the machine managed to avoid removing hazelnut spread from the blades. The cutlery basket was in the middle as always. What is the machine doing for two hours, how can you avoid rinsing hazelnut spread? And that's from all the blades. The model from the pre-series, which "only" held four place settings and lasted 15 years, was a thousand times better. Maybe a little louder. With this machine, someone was determined to keep the promise of six place settings, no matter what the result. The door seal gets dirty quickly on the left and right because the door doesn't fit properly. It only washes well if you don't fill it up. That may be why there are so many good reviews, which I don't understand. The next dishwasher will probably be a no-name one. What a pity.
Comments (Original): [ Keine Empfehlung ] || ---------------- || Habe das Gerät seit einigen Monaten in Betrieb. Größtes Manko: Das viel zu eng stehende Geschirr. Suppenteller mit Haferflockenresten werden nur sauber, wenn ich immer einen Stellplatz dazwischen frei lasse. Auch ein sofortiges Spülen hilft nicht, da kommt das Spülwasser scheinbar einfach nicht hin. Flachteller von Melitta Ceracron (leicht erhöhter Rand)passen gar nicht rein. Der Abstand der Drähte ist zu gering! Habe das zu spät bemerkt, da ich es als Zweitgeschirr benutze. Die Ablage links lässt sich nur auf 45 Grad arretieren, so dass man beim Einräumen ständig hängen bleibt. Was hat die Konstrukteure da eigentlich geritten? Bei der Vorserie (Generation Piccolo) wo diese hinten waren konnte man die ganz hochklappen. Beim Auotmatikprogramm hat es die Maschine jetzt mal geschafft Nussnougatcreme auf den Messern nicht zu entfernen. Besteckkorb stand in der Mitte wie immer. Was macht die Maschine zwei Stunden lang, wie schafft man es Nussnougatcreme nicht abzuspülen? Und zwar an allen Messern. Das Modell der Vorserie, was 'nur' vier Maßgedecke fasste und 15 Jahre gehalten hat, war tausend Mal besser. Vielleicht etwas lauter. Bei dem gerät hier hat mal wohl auf Teufel komm raus das sechs Maßgedeckeversprechen einhalten wollen. Egal mit welchem Ergebnis. Die Türdichtung verschmutzt links und rechts schnell, weil die Tür da wohl nicht richtig anliegt. Gut Spülen tut sie nur, wenn man sie nicht voll macht. Daher vielleicht die mir unverständlicher Weise vielen guten Rezensionen.Die nächste Spülmaschine wird dann vermutlich Noname. Schade.

Sentence (English): Dishwasher looks great and is very quiet when it ran.
Comments (English): [ Awful Lowes and Bosch experience ] || ---------------- || Dishwasher looks great and is very quiet when it ran. However, it started leaking during its first run. We purchased on February 27th, the unit was delivered to Lowes on March 10th and installed on March 15th. I had removed the old unit, so it was a quick install. Unfortunately, the installers never turned on the water. I didn't run a load until the following Sunday and it leaked that day. I called the installer company, they came back out on March 26th to confirm it was not their issue with the connections, it was a failure in the unit and this was the second one they had seen in two weeks. They confirmed it would be a swap, gave me a work order and Lowes would be in touch soon. Two days later, Lowes calls and informs me because the issue occurred after 48 hours after the installation, I would have to call Bosch service. After about 20 minutes of debate, they approved a new unit. Two days later, I receive another call from Lowes saying the same thing (as though I had never talked to them). After another 20 minutes and confirming I made the purchase on my Lowe's card, they once again agreed to swap the unit out. On April 10th, a new unit was finally delivered to Lowe's and the new installation will occur on Tuesday April 16th. nearly two months later. I will update once the new unit is in place, but so far, an awful experience with Lowes and this particular "best of the best" dishwasher units.

Comments (English): [ I finally invited my aunt~! ^^ ] || ---------------- || Samsung Electronics Bespoke Kitchen Fit Built-in 14-Person Dishwasher. I wanted to free my husband from his main job of washing dishes. I bought one of my three great-aunts' dishwashers. I used it for a month at my sister's house abroad and it was incredibly convenient. There were many evenings when I really didn't want to do the dishes because they piled up, but now I can just collect them and do them all at once in the evening, which is incredibly convenient. At first, I felt guilty about collecting all the dishes like this, but I guess I'll get used to it. My sink is gray, so I ordered the Kota Charcoal one. After installing it, it camouflaged itself almost like a chameleon. It really looks like it was built right in. The sink repairman came a day after I ordered it, and the dishwasher installer came the next day, and the installation was quick and easy. The sink had to be cut, so there was an additional 90,000 won fee. The work took about an hour and a half. But even though they cleaned up the hallway and the front door, there was a lot of wood dust, so I had to wipe it with a wet tissue for 30 minutes. It would have been nice if they had laid down something like vinyl when working. That was the most disappointing part. The installation took about 30 minutes, and they gave me an explanation before leaving~~. After using it, I regret why I didn't buy it sooner. It's really, really convenient! It has many functions, but I mainly use the standard course. I also use the strong dry function occasionally. Sentence (English): Read plenty of reviews of models from various manufacturers, including ratings from Consumers Reports.
Comments (English): [ Expensive but might be worth it ] || ---------------- || Read plenty of reviews of models from various manufacturers, including ratings from Consumers Reports. I tended to disregard any review that was "sponsored" or compensated in any way by the manufacturer. Quite frankly, most models by most manufacturers seemed to be unreliable, of low quality, and unsatisfactory to their owners. As the very satisfied owner of several Bosch power tools, I leaned towards the Bosch models and Consumer Reports rated them the highest in reliability and owner satisfaction. But reviews I read on multiple sites held much more negative opinions of the Bosch 100/300/500/800 series models, rating them no better than their competitors. None of the local stores carried the more expensive Benchmark series and I couldn't find many trustworthy reviews but I decided to gamble on the higher priced model and couldn't be more satisfied so far. The one obvious shortcoming is the diminutive size of the silverware basket, it is laughably small. However, I'd read a review where an owner stressed the importance of keeping the larger basket from your old dishwasher and using it in the new Benchmark. I had to modify the lower rack slightly by cutting a couple of tines to make it fit but that was a small price to pay for keeping a reasonable sized basket. It seems all Bosch models, with the exception of the even pricier $2400 Benchmark model, have these tiny baskets. We've had the dishwasher for two months and are completely satisfied with it's cleaning and drying performance. It's 38 db noise claim appears to be accurate, you can't hear it while standing in front of it unless it's on the drain cycle and even then it's barely audible. I've set up the phone app that can monitor or control it wirelessly but find no use for that convenience, others might. Our Benchmark has more loading options and the middle rack definitely holds more items than our old model. The top and bottom racks seem comparable in capacity to our old GE now that we've replaced the silverware basket. So, we've paid twice as much as planned for a new dishwasher but appear to have gotten what we paid for. Based on our two month experience, I would highly recommend the Benchmark series.

As the very satisfied owner of several Bosch power tools, I leaned towards the Bosch models and Consumer Reports rated them the highest in reliability and owner satisfaction. But reviews I read on multiple sites held much more negative opinions of the Bosch 100/300/500/800 series models, rating them no better than their competitors. None of the local stores carried the more expensive Benchmark series and I couldn't find many trustworthy reviews but I decided to gamble on the higher priced model and couldn't be more satisfied so far. The one obvious shortcoming is the diminutive size of the silverware basket, it is laughably small. However, I'd read a review where an owner stressed the importance of keeping the larger basket from your old dishwasher and using it in the new Benchmark. I had to modify the lower rack slightly by cutting a couple of tines to make it fit but that was a small price to pay for keeping a reasonable sized basket. It seems all Bosch models, with the exception of the even pricier $2400 Benchmark model, have these tiny baskets. We've had the dishwasher for two months and are completely satisfied with it's cleaning and drying performance. It's 38 db noise claim appears to be accurate, you can't hear it while standing in front of it unless it's on the drain cycle and even then it's barely audible. I've set up the phone app that can monitor or control it wirelessly but find no use for that convenience, others might. Our Benchmark has more loading options and the middle rack definitely holds more items than our old model. The top and bottom racks seem comparable in capacity to our old GE now that we've replaced the silverware basket. So, we've paid twice as much as planned for a new dishwasher but appear to have gotten what we paid for. Based on our two month experience, I would highly recommend the Benchmark series.

Comments (English): [ A Seamless Transition ] || ---------------- || For over two decades, I've been a loyal owner of Fisher Paykel innovative two-drawer dishwasher. So, when the time came to switch to a Bosch dishwasher, I approached the change with caution. However, any reservations I had were swiftly dispelled upon experiencing the seamless performance of the Bosch appliance. First and foremost, the standout feature of the Bosch is its near-silent operation. As someone accustomed to the discreet hum of my previous appliance, the virtually soundless performance of the Bosch was a pleasant surprise. This not only enhances the tranquilty of my kitchen space but also speaks volumes about the quality of its engineering. Although, I do wish it had a timer (on the front) to see how long is left in the cycle. Beyound its whisper-quiet operation, the Bosch dishwasher delivers on all fronts of functionality and efficiency. Its intuitive design ensures that every dish, glass, and utensil emerges sparkling clean, regardless of the load size of grime. The variety of wash cycles and customizable settings cater to diverse needs, from my delicate stemware to heavily soiled plates. In terms of durability and longevity, I have only had for two months, that it proves to be a worthy investment. So far it has exceeded my expectations. Like any diswasher it is an indispensable asset in a kitchen. I highly recommend to anyone in search of a top-tier dishwashing experience.
